name: sieger1010/h2a
what_it_holds: Standardized U.S. Department of Labor H-2A agricultural seasonal-worker employment disclosure data, FY2008 through FY2025 Q3 (17+ years). Processed exports in processed_exports/ as CSV, Pickle, Feather, Parquet, and a SQLite DB. Fields include employer name (with known aliasing issues, e.g. North Carolina Growers Association), wage data, work-site location, employment start/end dates, worker certification counts, and DOL case numbers (some duplicated). README notes reported fields change across years so YoY comparisons need care; Python cleaning scripts are in-repo.
why_useful: H-2A is a seasonal-migrant-worker visa program tied to harvest calendars in specific U.S. counties/states; a point-in-time, multi-year, county-level labor inflow series is a proxy for seasonal rural/agricultural-region short-term-rental and worker-housing demand (relevant to niche STR demand pockets and to broader seasonal-labor-market strength as a consumer-spending input) rather than a direct ABNB KPI driver, but it is a genuinely large, long, well-processed public dataset with no equivalent already held.

name: pegeler/unemployment (LAUS annual averages)
what_it_holds: R package bundling BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS) annual averages 1990-2017 as a data.frame: 90,088 rows x 9 columns (LAUS code, state/county FIPS, county name, year, labor force, employment, unemployment level, unemployment rate) at county/metro-area level.
why_useful: Fills the 'unemployment by metro' curated-panel ask directly: county-level history back to 1990 committed as data, no API key needed, usable as a regional consumer-strength control for NA nights/ADR.

name: blscrapeR
what_it_holds: R package/API client wrapping the BLS API: state- and metro-area unemployment (LAUS) via county_fips()/quick_unemp_rate(), CPI/inflation adjustment functions using CPI data from 1947 onward (inflation_adjust()), quick_employed_level(), quick_laborForce_rate(); CRAN package, 381 commits, actively maintained.
why_useful: One-command pull for metro unemployment and long-run CPI (1947+) matching the theme's 'unemployment by metro' and 'CPI' asks; more turnkey than raw BLS API for regional consumer-strength splits (NA/EMEA proxy via US metro cuts).
time_coverage: CPI from 1947; unemployment current + historical via API
duplicate_of_holding: overlaps our existing BLS CPI holding; adds LAUS metro convenience layer
